How Action Items Are Classified
GoalThe what — desired outcome. Keywords: reach, earn, save, lose, become, complete, achieve, grow, read, travel, visit. Contains Projects and Tasks.
ProjectThe how — multi-step effort. Keywords: plan, design, launch, build, set up, organize, redesign, implement, create, develop. Contains Tasks, links to Goals.
TaskThe do — single discrete action. Binary: done or not done. Rolls up to Projects and Goals.
Use Reclassify to cycle through types after analyzing.
Quick Classification Test
🎯 Goal — "WHAT do I want to achieve?"
☐ Outcome-based (a result or vision)?
☐ Measurable and time-bound?
☐ Months/years to complete?
☐ Needs multiple projects?
📁 Project — "HOW will I make it happen?"
☐ Clear deliverable or product?
☐ Weeks/months to complete?
☐ Rolls into a Goal?
☐ Made up of multiple tasks?
✅ Task — "DO it. Single action."
One action. Binary: done or not done. Can be completed in one session. No sub-steps.

Full core-field import: columns are case-insensitive and can be in any order. Only Name is required. Lists, Categories, Planning Stage, and Effort are controlled values — invalid values are blocked rather than added.
Recognized core columns: Name, Type, Status, Level, Planning Stage, Effort, Priority, Start Date, Target/Due Date, Completed Date, Estimated Minutes, Screen Time Required, Duration, Duration Unit, List(s), Categories, Tags, Sequence Number, Sprint, Rotation Week, Focus Periods, Check-in Date, Budget, Blockers, On Hold Reason, Cancellation Reason, Reference Link, Notes, Function, Cadence, Knowledge Type, Maintenance Type, Linked Item, Habit Frequency, Habit Time, Habit Routine, Habit Amount Min, Habit Amount Target, Habit Amount Stretch, Habit Amount Unit, Habit Cue Type, Habit Cue Detail, Habit Friction, Habit Health Metric, Habit Challenge Target %.
Linked Item hierarchy: use the exact parent Action Item name. Recommended structure is Goal → Project → Phase → Task (or Goal → Phase → Task when no Project is needed). A Phase must link to a Goal or Project. When phases are used, link each Task to its respective Phase rather than only to the top-level Project/Goal. Parent and child rows can be in the same file; Bulk Add creates them in hierarchy order automatically.
For Lists, Categories, Tags, and Focus Periods, separate multiple values with a semicolon (;). Blank cells fall back to the shared Bulk Add fields above when one exists.
Content rows: when Type = content, you can also import Content Type, Stage, Purpose, Pillar, Campaign, Audience, Offer, CTA, Platforms, Brand, Publish Date, family-specific writing fields, document fields, and content performance metrics.
Select items to update. Only fields you fill in will be changed. Empty fields are skipped.
